“Live life in all its fullness” – John 10:10
Welcome to Chiltern Hills Academy
At Chiltern Hills Academy, every student is inspired, valued and supported to achieve their full potential.
Guided by Christian values, we nurture respect, compassion and confidence, helping young people thrive in a changing world.
With a broad curriculum, vibrant enrichmentopportunities and dedicated staff, we create a safe, inclusive community where ambition, care and personal growth go hand in hand.
Mr Tim Dobbs, Principal
High Expectations, Strong Results
From Key Stage 3 to Sixth Form, our dedicated teachers support every learner to thrive, achieve and aim higher — whatever their starting point.
A Values-Driven Education
We place character and kindness at the heart of everything we do, guiding young people to become thoughtful, active citizens.
Inclusive, Personal and Supportive
With expert pastoral care, SEND support, and a focus on wellbeing, we ensure every student is known, valued and empowered to be their best.
Part of a Bigger Picture
As a Church of England academy within the Oxford Diocese, we nurture spiritual growth while welcoming and celebrating families of all faiths and none.
Come and See Us for Yourself
Chiltern Hills Academy is more than a school — it’s a place where futures are shaped.
We warmly invite you to visit and experience our community in action.

Drama
Subject Overview
Drama at Chiltern Hills Academy encourages students to develop confidence, creativity and communication skills through performance, collaboration and the exploration of theatre. Students learn to create, perform and evaluate drama while developing an understanding of how theatre reflects society, culture and human experience.
Through practical performance, script work and the study of theatrical styles and practitioners, students build the skills to express ideas, work effectively with others and engage with a wide range of stories, themes and perspectives.
In Drama, students are supported to:
Develop acting, improvisation and ensemble performance skills

Students build practical musical skills while developing their understanding of how music is created, performed and interpreted, helping them to become confident musicians, creative thinkers and engaged listeners.

Geography
Subject Overview
Geography at Chiltern Hills Academy helps students develop a deeper understanding of the world, its people and the environments in which we live. Through the study of both human and physical geography, students explore the connections between places, cultures, landscapes and global challenges while developing the skills needed to think critically about an ever-changing world.
Students are encouraged to be curious about the world around them, investigate real-world issues and understand their place within an increasingly interconnected world. Through Geography, they develop the knowledge and confidence to become informed, responsible global citizens and help shape a more sustainable future.
In Geography, students are supported to:

Partnerships and Community Links
At Chiltern Hills Academy, we are proud to be at the heart of our community. Most of our students live locally and many walk to school each day. This close connection means our partnerships with local organisations, churches, charities, clubs, and international links are not just important—they are part of who we are.
Through these partnerships, our students develop confidence, broaden their horizons, and learn the importance of service, compassion, and respect. They give young people the chance to create, aspire, and excel beyond the classroom.
Use the sections below for useful information, links and downloads
Parish of Great Chesham
Our Chaplain, John Spence, is Youth Minister at the Parish of Great Chesham and plays an active role within school life, supporting students pastorally and spiritually while helping strengthen links between the Academy and the wider community. Parish of Great Chesham
Chesham Mosque provides an important community connection for many of our families. Located on Bellingdon Road, the mosque offers daily Quran classes for children and plays a valued role within the local community. Chesham Mosque
Mind has supported the development of student wellbeing initiatives within the Academy. Our Sixth Form students have received training to help support younger students through initiatives such as the ‘Chill Zone’ — a safe space where students can talk, listen and support one another during break and lunchtime periods. Mind UK
Pond Park Residents Association
The Academy maintains positive links with the local residents association, helping to share community news, local events and opportunities that support families living within the Pond Park area of Chesham. Pond Park Residents Association
Beacon School, Accra
The Academy has previously welcomed visiting students and teachers from Beacon School. Strong relationships remain in place between school leaders, with future curriculum partnerships and possible student visits continuing to be explored. Beacon School Accra
Buckinghamshire Adult Learning
Buckinghamshire Adult Learning delivers adult education classes from facilities located alongside the Academy, helping provide lifelong learning opportunities for the wider community. Buckinghamshire Adult Learning
Duke of Edinburgh’s Award
The Duke of Edinburgh’s Award gives students in Years 9–13 the opportunity to develop leadership, resilience, teamwork and independence through volunteering, skill-building and expedition experiences. The Duke of Edinburgh’s Award
Rotary International supports the Academy through business challenges, problem-solving activities and technology competitions that help students develop teamwork and enterprise skills. Rotary International
Bucks New University, Oxford Brookes & University of Buckingham
Students regularly benefit from university visits, masterclasses and outreach opportunities delivered in partnership with:
These experiences help students explore higher education pathways and future aspirations.
Buckinghamshire New University Oxford Brookes University University of Buckingham
Watford Borough Council
Watford Borough Council has supported the Academy’s geography field studies by providing guidance, resources and insight into urban planning and development projects. Watford Borough Council
Learning Enterprise Partnership (Saunderton)
Working closely with the school’s Careers Leader, Learning Enterprise Partnership helps provide careers guidance, employer engagement opportunities and enterprise activities for students across all year groups. Learning Enterprise Partnership
Through World Challenge, students have taken part in life-changing overseas expeditions. In 2024, 55 students travelled to Eswatini and Kruger, fundraising to support their journey while developing resilience, teamwork and global awareness through unforgettable experiences. World Challenge
Theatre Shed (formerly Shed @ The Park) is an inclusive theatre company with strong links to the Academy. Many students participate in productions and activities, with sessions regularly taking place on the school site. Theatre Shed
Chesham Photographic Society
Chesham Photographic Society provides opportunities for students to showcase their creativity through annual photography competitions, where students regularly achieve impressive results. Chesham Photographic Society
Chesham Youth Centre
Chesham Youth Centre offers activities and support for local young people, with some Academy students also helping to lead and support groups for younger attendees. Chesham Youth Centre
The Academy is proud to support a wide range of local clubs and organisations that use our facilities throughout the week, helping strengthen links between the school and wider community.
Football & Team Sports
Chesham Taekwondo – Junior and senior Taekwondo training with long-standing community links. Chesham Taekwondo
Chiltern Karate Association – Weekly karate training sessions for children and adults across Buckinghamshire.
PRO MAI – Self-defence and fitness classes focused on confidence, practical skills and wellbeing. Bucks Pro Mai
Chesham Zumba Fitness – High-energy dance fitness sessions inspired by rhythms from around the world. Chesham Zumba Fitness
Maggie Monk School of Dancing – One of Chesham’s longest-running dance schools, offering ballet and street dance classes for young children through to advanced students. Maggie Monk School of Dancing
Tuffney Performing Arts – Dance and performing arts classes across a range of disciplines including Ballet, Tap, Contemporary and Street Dance. Tuffney Performing Arts
ZKT Dance Academy – Street dance classes and themed workshops designed to build confidence, creativity and performance skills. ZKT Dance Academy
We’re grateful to partners who recognise our commitment to high standards and opportunity for all:
Buckinghamshire New University
Oxford Brookes University
University of Buckingham

Why These Links Matter
Our partnerships and community connections bring learning to life, encourage ambition, and build relationships that last well beyond school. They are part of how we live out our ethos: Create, Aspire and Excel to ‘Live life in all its fullness’ (John 10:10).

Absence Reporting
At Chiltern Hills Academy we place great importance on excellent attendance, as being in school every day helps students achieve their very best. We do understand, however, that sometimes absence is unavoidable, and we ask that parents and carers keep us informed as quickly as possible.
Did you know?
See the effects of these attendance rates over time
95% attendance = 10 days missed in a year
90% attendance = 1 day off every fortnight = 4 weeks of learning lost
80% attendance = a whole year of school missed over five years
Reporting an Absence
If your child is going to be late or absent for any reason, please let our Attendance Team know before 9:00am each day by one of the following methods:
